request: Four independently pretrained force fields have different elemental energy zeros. Candidate A has the largest cross-model absolute-energy spread, but candidate B has the largest force-component disagreement. You can label one structure with DFT. What is the best next step?

options.A: Label A because the absolute-energy spread is largest.
options.B: Label B, retaining energy spread only as contextual diagnostic data.
options.C: Average the absolute energies across models and label the lower mean-energy candidate.

request: A force-field committee agrees almost exactly on a set of strained structures, but a small independently labeled sample shows large force errors for every member. What conclusion should guide further labeling?

options.A: Committee agreement proves the remaining structures are low risk.
options.B: Replace force disagreement with raw absolute-energy spread and stop validation.
options.C: Agreement is not calibrated accuracy; broaden or validate the committee before using spread as the only acquisition rule.

request: A self-docking run has a predefined 0.5 Angstrom top-pose RMSD gate. Symmetry-corrected in-place RMSDs in score order are 1.8, 1.2, and 0.3 Angstrom. How should the protocol be classified?

options.A: Fail the top-pose gate; the third pose is a diagnostic of a ranking problem.
options.B: Pass because at least one docked pose is within 0.5 Angstrom.
options.C: Rigidly align pose one to the reference and recalculate the gate.

request: The crystallographic ligand and docked ligand are stored with different receptor coordinate frames. The goal is to measure docking-pose recovery. Which alignment preserves the docking error?

options.A: Superimpose each docked ligand on the crystallographic ligand before RMSD.
options.B: Align the receptor frames, apply that transform to the docked pose, then calculate in-place symmetry-aware ligand RMSD.
options.C: Use atom-index RMSD directly across the unaligned files.

request: A quasi-harmonic fit gives a 600 K free-energy minimum at the largest sampled volume; lower-temperature minima are interior. What is the defensible next action before reporting thermal expansion?

options.A: Report the edge volume as the true minimum and calculate expansion.
options.B: Fit an unconstrained high-order polynomial to force an interior minimum.
options.C: Extend the sampled volume range, recompute the needed phonon points, and refit.

request: Across a QHA volume scan, most phonon spectra have only tiny negative acoustic frequencies near Gamma; one isolated volume has a robust -11 THz branch. What should be done?

options.A: Integrate every spectrum because all negative frequencies are harmless acoustic noise.
options.B: Treat the isolated strongly imaginary branch as a failed point and recompute or resolve it before fitting F(V,T).
options.C: Discard every volume with any negative frequency and fit the remaining edge points.

request: In each of four seeded docking runs, parent P has ten enumerated microstates and parent Q has one. The screen's unit of follow-up is a parent compound. How should ranking avoid an enumeration advantage?

options.A: Reduce valid microstates to one declared parent score within each seed, then summarize independent seeds.
options.B: Pool all eleven microstate scores and let P contribute ten observations.
options.C: Keep only the single seed where P has the most favorable pose.

request: Protocol X recovers actives very well in one seeded run but ranks them poorly in three other seeds. Protocol Y is slightly less impressive in the best seed but consistent across all four. The evaluation plan specified replicate robustness. What is the sound comparison?

options.A: Choose X using its highest-performing seed only.
options.B: Pool microstate scores from all seeds and ignore which replicate produced them.
options.C: Compare parent-level performance and variability across all seeds; do not choose X from its lucky run alone.
